rows.note: This is the all-purpose choice for disagreeing with or opposing a person, idea, or proposal.

example.jyutping: ngo5 faan2 deoi3 ni1 go3 tai4 ji5

rows.note: Use this when the opposition is expressed as a protest, especially against something seen as unfair or unacceptable.

example.english: I object to the company suddenly docking my pay.
example.traditional: 我抗議公司無啦啦扣我人工。
example.jyutping: ngo5 kong3 ji5 gung1 si1 mou4 laa1 laa1 kau3 ngo5 jan4 gung1

rows.note: Use this formal phrase when raising an objection in a court or other official proceeding.

example.english: The defense immediately rose to object.
example.jyutping: bin6 fong1 zik1 si4 tai4 ceot1 ji6 ji5

rows.note: Use 嘢 as the all-purpose spoken word for a physical, inanimate thing.

example.jyutping: go2 gin6 je5 m4 hou2 baai2 hai2 dou6

rows.note: Use 問題 when the object is an issue or problem attracting attention or concern.

example.english: The upstairs noise has become an object of concern for the neighbours.
example.traditional: 樓上啲噪音已經成為鄰居關注嘅問題。
example.jyutping: lau4 soeng6 di1 cou3 jam1 ji5 ging1 sing4 wai4 leon4 gei1 gwaan1 zyu3 ge3 man6 tai4

rows.note: Use 對象 for the person or thing toward which a feeling is directed, especially a romantic interest or emotional target.

example.english: They are the object of my affection; I've had a crush on them for ages.
example.traditional: 佢係我暗戀咗好耐嘅對象。
example.jyutping: keoi5 hai6 ngo5 am3 lyun2 zo2 hou2 noi6 ge3 deoi3 zoeng6
